issues.legal_issue: A first appellate court hearing an appeal from an original decree must reconsider the issues of law and fact raised in the appeal and give a reasoned decision on them, and a cryptic affirmance that does not do so must be set aside and remanded.
material_facts: The trial court dismissed a specific-performance suit after finding that it was time-barred and that the plaintiff was not ready and willing to perform the contract.
The first appeal raised questions of law and fact, including limitation and readiness and willingness.
The High Court affirmed the trial court by a cryptic order without reappreciating the evidence or examining those issues.
issues.conclusion: The High Court’s judgment and decree were set aside, and the matter was remanded to it for fresh disposal in accordance with law; the parties’ contentions remained open.
issues.legal_principle: Under Section 96 of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908, a first appeal is a continuation of the original proceedings and ordinarily permits rehearing on fact and law. Order XLI Rule 31 requires the appellate judgment to state the points for determination, the decision on them, and the reasons. Those requirements apply even when the appellate court affirms the trial court; if it agrees with the trial court’s views on the evidence, a general expression of agreement with the reasons may ordinarily suffice. The court relied on Hari Shankar v. Rao Girdhari Lal Chowdhury; Shankar Ramchandra Abhyankar v. Krishnaji Dattatreya Bapat; Santosh Hazari v. Purushottam Tiwari; Madhukar v. Sangram; B. M. Narayana Gowda v. Shanthamma; H. K. N. Swami v. Irshad Basith; M/s. Sri Raja Lakshmi Dyeing Works v. Rangaswamy Chettiar; Vinod Kumar v. Gangadhar; and Shasidhar v. Ashwani Uma Mathad. The court distinguished a first appeal from a second appeal, for which Section 100 limits the appeal to a substantial question of law.

rule.if: first_appeal_from_original_decree and appeal_involves_questions_of_law_or_fact and appellate_court_gives_cryptic_affirmance and appellate_court_does_not_examine_issues_or_evidence

predicates.first_appeal_from_original_decree: An aggrieved party brings a first appeal from a decree made by a court exercising original jurisdiction.
predicates.appeal_involves_questions_of_law_or_fact: The appeal raises questions of law or fact for the appellate court to decide.
predicates.appellate_court_gives_cryptic_affirmance: The appellate court affirms the decree in an order that does not meaningfully state its determination and reasons.
predicates.appellate_court_does_not_examine_issues_: The appellate court does not examine the issues raised or the evidence relevant to them.

issues.definition: When a first appeal from an original decree raises issues for decision but the appellate court affirms without meaningfully examining those issues or the evidence and giving reasons, the appellate judgment is set aside and the case is remanded.
